title: Discharge temperature too high
meaning: The compressed air leaving the machine is hotter than normal. Heat is the most common early sign of a struggling compressor.
likely_causes: Cooler fins are blocked with dust or dirt
Cooling fan is slow or stopped
Room is too hot or has poor air flow
fix_steps: Stop the compressor and let it cool down.
Isolate the power and release the air pressure before opening any panel.
Check the oil level and top up if it is low.
Clean the cooler fins and the air inlet.
Check that the cooling fan turns freely.
Restart and watch the temperature for 15 minutes.
safety_note: Hot surfaces and stored pressure can injure. Only a trained person should open the machine.

title: Oil level or oil pressure low
meaning: There may not be enough oil to protect the moving parts. Running like this can wreck the compressor block.
likely_causes: Oil has leaked or been used up
fix_steps: Stop the compressor straight away.
Isolate the power and release the air pressure.
Check the oil level and look for leaks around the pipes and filter.
Top up with the oil type the manufacturer specifies.
If the level is fine, replace the oil filter and call a service engineer.
safety_note: Do not restart until the oil problem is understood.

title: Motor current too high
meaning: The motor is pulling more electricity than normal. The machine is working too hard or something is dragging.
likely_causes: Air filter or separator is blocked
Machine is overloaded by air demand
fix_steps: Check whether air demand has risen suddenly.
Inspect the air filter and separator and clean or replace them.
Listen and feel for rough or noisy bearings.
Ask an electrician to check the supply voltage.
Call a service engineer if the current stays high.
safety_note: Only a qualified electrician should work on the electrical supply.

title: Air filter needs service
meaning: The air filter is getting clogged, so the machine has to work harder to breathe in.
likely_causes: Filter is past its service interval
fix_steps: Plan the filter change for the next convenient stop.
Isolate the power and release the air pressure.
Replace the filter with the correct part.
Reset the service counter after the job.

title: Vibration higher than normal
meaning: The machine is shaking more than it did when healthy. This often shows up days before a bearing or mounting problem causes a fault code.
fix_steps: Note the time and load when it started.
Check that the mounting bolts and guards are tight.
Listen for grinding or squealing near the motor and the compressor block.
Book a bearing inspection before the next scheduled shutdown.
safety_note: Keep hands and clothing away from moving parts while checking.

title: Humidity and rust risk high
meaning: Salty, damp air around the machine raises the risk of corrosion on electrical parts and the cooler.
likely_causes: Poor ventilation or a gap in the enclosure
fix_steps: Check that panel doors and seals close properly.
Wipe away any moisture or salt deposits.
Improve ventilation or add a dehumidifier if it keeps happening.
Inspect electrical terminals for rust at the next service.
